name: YouTube how-to topic search with filters and transcript precheck
goal: Find distillable how-to YouTube videos for a topic across several languages, filter by duration, upload recency, views and how-to title signals, and precheck which ones have a Show transcript (manual, auto, AI-dub, or YouTube-translatable to English) before anything is fetched. Delta vs generic youtube search skills (e.g. VoltAgent youtube-skills, last30days-skill): multilingual how-to keyword expansion, negative-signal filtering, and a per-video transcript-track precheck that feeds the knowledge-pipeline router.
prerequisites: Pipeline venv /workspace/skill-library/.venv with yt-dlp and youtube-transcript-api (scripts/ensure_env.sh rebuilds it)

inputs.name: topic
inputs.description: Topic words, e.g. 'cinematic pad sound design'

inputs.name: langs
inputs.description: Comma list of query languages (en,de,es,ja,fr,pt); each adds its own how-to keywords

outputs.name: search_results
outputs.description: pipeline/searches/<date>-<slug>.json: ranked results with howto_score, transcript precheck, and a dropped list with reasons

constraints: Transcript source is YouTube's Show transcript panel text (info section -> Transcript); say 'transcript', not 'captions'. Caption-file transports (.srt/.vtt) are only used internally and deleted.
Never invent transcript text, steps, or settings; every downstream fact must trace to a transcript timestamp.
No Whisper/ASR on the audio unless Matt explicitly asks; the router may only FLAG it as a last resort.
Search only; do not fetch transcript bodies at this stage (stage 1 of the distillery). Stop for confirmation unless Matt authorized an ongoing distillery run.
Titles can be YouTube auto-translated; do not infer the spoken language from the title. The precheck's track list and the fetcher's yt-dlp probe decide the language.
Space out prechecks (0.5 s+) and keep batches small; YouTube rate-limits bursts from cloud IPs.

steps.action: For each language in --langs, build a query of topic + that language's how-to keywords (en 'tutorial how to', de 'tutorial anleitung deutsch', es 'tutorial cómo español', ja '使い方 作り方 解説') and run yt-dlp flat search (ytsearchN, or the results URL with an sp= upload-date filter when --within is set).
steps.expect: Deduplicated candidate list with id, title, channel, duration, view_count

steps.action: Drop results outside duration bounds (Shorts under 3 min, multi-hour streams), under --min-views, with negative title signals (#shorts, reaction, unboxing, preset/sample pack, live stream, review, trailer), or already known (raw/ dir or LIBRARY.json) when --skip-known.
steps.expect: Every drop recorded with its reason

steps.action: Score the rest: +2 per how-to signal in the title (how to, tutorial, step by step, explained, from scratch, anleitung, cómo, 作り方, 音作り), +1 per topic word, +1.5 for a 5-30 min runtime, +log10(views)/2 capped at 3, -4 per negative signal. Sort descending.

With --precheck, list transcript tracks for the top results (youtube-transcript-api list only, no fetch). Record has_transcript, manual languages, auto languages, auto_dub_suspected (more than 3 auto tracks = YouTube AI dubbing), english_direct, and yt_translate_to_en.
steps.expect: Each kept result shows [T: manual/auto langs; yt->en] or [no transcript]

steps.action: With --require-transcript, drop results with no track and log why (transcripts_disabled, video_unavailable, rate_limited). Save JSON to pipeline/searches/ and hand the ids to youtube-knowledge-pipeline-router.
steps.expect: Saved file path printed; ids ready for routing

verification: Saved JSON has results[] with howto_score and transcript fields, plus dropped[] with reasons
No kept result is a Short (<180 s) or has a negative title signal
With --require-transcript every kept result has transcript.has_transcript == true
